title: Ines and the Oath
premise: Marguerite Coldharbour, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the pieces he carves, has hidden his gift for a decade in Vellamark, where magic is outlawed and the crown's new Hunt burns the gifted in the market square. When a dying soldier presses an oath-bone into his hands—a relic binding King Aldric to a crown-spirit that devours kings from within—Marguerite becomes the only person who can unbind the monarch before the spirit fully wears him. Guided by Ines, a disgraced royal oath-keeper who once helped forge the binding and now wants her name cleared, Marguerite must gather three lost bone-vessels while evading the Hunt's ruthless captain, who suspects him at every turn. At the winter coronation renewal, Marguerite chooses to pour his own memories of Ines into the unbinding rite—sacrificing their shared past to free the king—and ends the book with the kingdom saved, the Hunt dissolved, and two strangers who feel they've loved each other beginning again.
about_author: J. M. Ashgrove is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing funeral effigies in northern cathedral crypts, an experience that seeped into every page of this debut. They write in a drafty stone cottage and claim, only half-jokingly, that the house remembers its previous owners.

chapters.title: The Quiet Trade
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He carves a mourning charm for a widow, hearing her dead husband's last words through the bone, and pockets the coin with practiced guilt. Establishes his double life: beloved craftsman by day, criminal by nature. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as routine.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Fountain
chapters.summary: Marguerite watches from a crowd as criers announce the Hunt for the gifted; a neighbor's apothecary is already marked with ash. His hands shake as he walks home past his own charms hanging in shop windows. Beat: safety curdling into fear.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He burns ten years of carved vessels in his hearth, but keeps one small whalebone piece he cannot explain his attachment to. A knock at the door sends him out the back window. Beat: severing the past, reluctantly.

chapters.title: The Soldier in the Alley
chapters.summary: A gut-wounded royal soldier finds Marguerite's hiding place and presses an oath-bone into his hands, whispering 'the king is not the king' before dying. The bone screams with layered voices. Beat: horror and unwanted destiny.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Captain Serane Voss POV. Introduce the Hunt's leader: pragmatic, not cruel, hunting the gifted because she watched magic kill her family. She examines the soldier's corpse and notes the missing relic. Beat: a worthy antagonist with her own grief.

chapters.title: Ines of the Broken Order
chapters.summary: Marguerite is ambushed by Ines, a former royal oath-keeper who recognizes the oath-bone. She demands it; he refuses; she saves him from a patrol anyway. Beat: wary alliance born of mutual leverage.

chapters.title: The History of the Binding
chapters.summary: Ines explains: forty years ago the Order bound a protective spirit to the crown; it has soured, devouring each king's mind. Unbinding requires three bone-vessels scattered after the Order's fall. Beat: the quest takes shape; Ines's guilt surfaces.

chapters.title: Market of Whispers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They seek the first vessel in a black-market reliquary beneath the tanneries, trading a carving for information. Marguerite realizes he enjoys being known for what he is. Beat: belonging, dangerous and sweet.

chapters.title: Voss Closes In
chapters.summary: Serane POV. Interrogation of the reliquary's owner yields a description of Marguerite. She posts his likeness, conflicted because the sketch shows kind eyes. Beat: hunter's doubt planted.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: First vessel recovered from a flooded chapel crypt; Marguerite must listen to hundreds of drowned dead to find it, nearly losing himself in their chorus. Ines pulls him back. Beat: the cost of his gift made visceral.

chapters.title: Two Travelers, One Fire
chapters.summary: Quiet interlude. Ines and Marguerite share histories by a fire; she reveals she forged the original binding as a young keeper who trusted the wrong mentor. Beat: intimacy growing alongside trust.

chapters.title: The King's Public Face
chapters.summary: Court observer POV via a minor noble Marguerite bribes. King Aldric appears lucid at council but claws at his crown when he thinks none watch. Beat: ticking clock established—the spirit nears full possession.

chapters.title: Roadblock at Greyford Bridge
chapters.summary: Hunt checkpoints seal the roads. Ines forges travel papers using her old seals; Marguerite charms a bored sergeant with a carved token. Beat: teamwork, and Marguerite realizing he'd follow her anywhere.

chapters.title: The Second Vessel's Keeper
chapters.summary: The second vessel belongs to a blind hermit who was once Ines's teacher—the mentor who soured the binding. He offers it freely, asking only forgiveness. Ines cannot speak. Marguerite forgives him in her place. Beat: mercy as theme.

chapters.title: Serane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Serane POV. She uncovers records proving the binding was corrupted deliberately, and her superiors order her to bury the evidence. Her faith in the crown cracks. Beat: antagonist begins turning.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Inn
chapters.summary: An informant sells their location; Hunt soldiers raid the inn. Ines is captured covering Marguerite's escape with the two vessels. Beat: devastating loss; Marguerite flees, hating himself.

chapters.title: Alone with the Voices
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Hiding in a charcoal burner's hut, he contemplates fleeing north but hears the dying soldier's voice in the oath-bone begging him to finish. Beat: despair transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Prison Under the Palace
chapters.summary: Ines POV in captivity. Serane visits her cell privately, not to torture but to ask questions. Ines gambles everything on the truth. Beat: unlikely understanding between prisoner and captor.

chapters.title: Bargaining with the Captain
chapters.summary: Marguerite turns himself in to reach Ines, offering Serane proof of the crown-spirit in exchange for access to the king. She gives him one night. Beat: audacity rewarded; stakes raised.

chapters.title: Audience with the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Marguerite is brought before Aldric. For one lucid minute the king begs for death or freedom; then the spirit speaks through him, promising Marguerite his heart's desire if he stops. Beat: temptation, and horror at the spirit's knowledge.

chapters.title: The Spirit's Offer
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The spirit shows him visions—including a future with Ines—in exchange for walking away. He refuses, and the spirit marks him, letting him leave so it can hunt him at leisure. Beat: false victory, dread.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Bone Gallery
chapters.summary: With Serane's tacit help, Marguerite frees Ines through the palace ossuary, where his gift lets him navigate by the dead's murmurs. Beat: thrilling escape; Serane officially becomes a traitor too.

chapters.title: Fugitives No More
chapters.summary: The trio camps in the hills. Serane shares her family's story; Ines finally names her mentor's betrayal aloud. Three broken people form a fragile fellowship. Beat: found belonging.

chapters.title: The Third Vessel's Price
chapters.summary: The final vessel lies in the Order's ruined motherhouse, warded so only an oath-keeper's blood opens it. Ines cuts deep; the ward drinks more than blood—it tests her worthiness with illusions. Beat: sacrifice and passage.

chapters.title: Illusions of the Motherhouse
chapters.summary: Inside the trial, Ines faces a life where she never joined the Order; Marguerite faces a life where he never hid. Each rejects the lie for the flawed truth. Beat: choosing reality over comfort—theme crystallized.

chapters.title: Three Vessels, One Rite
chapters.summary: The vessels assembled reveal the unbinding rite requires a memory of true love poured willingly into the bones. Marguerite and Ines realize what it will cost them—and hide it from each other. Beat: tragic dramatic irony.

chapters.title: Winter Coronation Eve
chapters.summary: The realm gathers for the Renewal, where the king re-swears his oath annually—the spirit's moment of greatest power and vulnerability. The city fills; the Hunt stands down for ceremony. Beat: calm before the storm.

chapters.title: Infiltrating the Procession
chapters.summary: Disguised among relic-bearers, the three enter the cathedral. Marguerite's marked skin burns as the spirit senses him. Beat: tension of concealment.

chapters.title: The Spirit Unmasked
chapters.summary: Mid-ceremony, the spirit abandons pretense, seizing Aldric's body publicly and turning the assembled nobility to stone-faced obedience. Chaos erupts; Serane holds off loyalist guards. Beat: open war.

chapters.title: The Rite Begins
chapters.summary: At the altar, Ines anchors the vessels while Marguerite channels the dead of the drowned chapel, the hermit, and every voice he's ever heard into a counter-song. Beat: overwhelming, transcendent effort.

chapters.title: What Memory Costs
chapters.summary: The rite stalls—it needs love's memory. Without telling Ines, Marguerite begins pouring out every moment they've shared. Ines understands too late and adds her own. Beat: heartbreaking climax of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax. The spirit, starved of the memories that fed it, is torn from Aldric and sealed into the emptied vessels. The king collapses, freed but broken. Marguerite and Ines stand over the bones as strangers. Beat: victory hollowed by loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Cathedral
chapters.summary: Aldric, lucid, abolishes the Hunt and restores the Order with Ines at its head. Serane is offered command of a reformed guard. Beat: justice and new purpose.

chapters.title: Strangers Who Remember Nothing
chapters.summary: Marguerite, memory-scoured of Ines, returns to his workshop. He finds a whalebone charm he doesn't remember keeping and weeps without knowing why. Beat: grief without a name.

chapters.title: The Body Remembers
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Leading the rebuilt Order, she visits Marguerite's shop under pretext of commissioning a memorial. Their hands brush; both feel lightning they can't source. Beat: hope flickering.

chapters.title: Carving What Cannot Be Forgotten
chapters.summary: Marguerite carves obsessively—faces, a bridge, a firelit camp—pieces his hands know but his mind doesn't. A customer recognizes Ines in one. Beat: the past resurfacing through craft.

chapters.title: The Oath Rekindled
chapters.summary: Ines brings him to the drowned chapel, hoping the dead will return what was given. Instead, Marguerite simply tells her: 'I don't remember you, but I think I loved you.' She answers: 'Then love me again.' Beat: emotional climax.

chapters.title: Beginning Again
chapters.summary: They court deliberately—two people falling in love a second time, telling each other the stories of what they lost. Marguerite discovers new memories forming where old ones were poured out. Beat: tender reconstruction.

chapters.title: The Charm on the Shelf
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Marguerite's POV. One year later: magic decriminalized, his shop openly a carver's haven, Ines arriving home. He finishes a new whalebone charm and, holding it, hears—for the first time—his own voice from the past saying her name. Beat: wholeness; memory and love reconciled.
